text:
Alex M: Quick proposal — add a 'sparse_capture' telemetry mode for high-volume routes. Instead of storing full req/resp bodies we store only request/response metadata + a short fingerprint (HMAC) or embedding-hash. Goal: reduce tokenized telemetry by ~90% for chatty endpoints.

Mari J: Love the idea. How would this interact with inspect/unmask flows? We still need to be able to pull full payloads for legal/debug when allowed. :thinking:

Alex M: Good point. Plan is: sparse_capture is the default capture policy for selected routes; inspect-mode can temporarily escalate to full capture but requires explicit audit log + breakglass. The console shows a per-tenant audit trail for any escalation.

Kevin P: Concern: PII detection. If we don't store bodies, we can't run downstream de-id or QA checks. Do we run a local PII detector before hashing?

Alex M: Yes — do PII heuristics inline in the ingest path, then:
1) If PII detected and tenant opted-out, redact and still emit sparse fingerprint.
2) If PII detected and tenant has inspect-policy, we annotate the capture record and mark for manual review.

Sophie L: UX question — console needs to make tradeoffs visible. Operators should see estimated monthly token savings, and a preview button that shows a synthetic redacted snapshot, not real data. Also add toggle per-route and a global safety cap.

Alex M: Wire config snippet for canary: 
```yaml
routes:
  - name: /api/chat
    capture_mode: sparse
    sample_rate: 0.02  # 2% full capture fallback for QA
    allow_inspect: true
```

Kevin P: The 2% full-capture fallback is smart for QA. We should make the fallback deterministic (hash-based) so replays correlate across logs. Also we need a rotating salt and key-rotation story for the HMACs.

Mari J: Also: quotas. If sparse_capture reduces token accounting for telemetry, that changes our tenant quota calculations. We need an explicit mapping in billing / quota pipeline: telemetry_token_equivalent = fingerprint_units + metadata_units. Show both raw tokens and normalized units in console.

Sophie L: Rollout plan idea: start with internal tenants + sign-up beta. Console UI: a "Simulate Savings" button that runs a dry-run for last 7 days and shows per-route savings + any lost debug coverage.

Kevin P: Security: hashed fingerprints must be non-reversible and + namespace per-tenant. Use HMAC-SHA256 with tenant salt stored in KMS. Add a TTL/rotate policy. Documented in the compliance playbook.

Alex M: Edge cases: attachments/embeddings — for attachments we only keep mime-type+size unless tenant opts-in. For embeddings we can keep the embedding vector fingerprint (quantized) not raw text.

Mari J: Monitoring: add dashboard panels for "debug coverage" (fraction of requests with full capture) and "sparse_capture_error_rate" (failures when running inline PII detector or HMAC). If error spikes, we should auto-fallback to full capture and alert on-call.

Sophie L: UX for rollouts: provide a canary slider (0-100%) per-route in console, plus a quota-warning banner if a tenant's debug coverage drops below SLA.

ops-bot: deploy-bot started canary for feature/telemetry/sparse-capture on infra-canary-3

Kevin P: One more: developer API. SDKs should provide an opt-in header `X-telemetry-verbosity: full|sparse|none`. Validate it against tenant policy server to avoid abuse.

Alex M: Next steps: write a short RFC (architecture + compliance appendix), implement a dry-run mode in ingest (no-op fingerprints, compute savings), and add console mockups. I'll open the RFC tomorrow. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
